page.title: Devices
page.subtitle: Connected keyboards and mice, hardware effects, the virtual desk and device bridges.
page.noneText: Plug in a supported keyboard or mouse. Missing yours? The wizard maps it in a few minutes.
page.hardwareHint: Runs on the device itself, without KeyHalo.
page.saveOnboardHint: Store a hardware effect in onboard memory so the device keeps it without KeyHalo running.
page.saveOnboardPick: Pick a hardware effect first (or give the active profile an onboard effect).
page.savedOnboard: Saved to the device's onboard memory
page.restoreText: Write back the settings {name} had the first time KeyHalo saw it (effect, brightness, DPI and polling). Your KeyHalo profiles are not touched.
page.deskHint: Drag devices to where they sit on your desk — synced effects flow across them.
page.deskEmpty: Connect a device to arrange your desk.
page.unknownHint: HID devices no definition recognises yet.
page.unknownNone: Every connected HID device is recognised.
page.lampCount: {n} LampArray devices found · {used} driven through it
page.bridgesNote: Razer devices are driven natively; their Dynamic Lighting interface is skipped so two apps never fight over the LEDs.

wiz.title: Add a device
wiz.subtitle: Map an unrecognised keyboard LED by LED and share the definition with everyone. Nothing is flashed: KeyHalo only lights LEDs.
wiz.pickHint: Unrecognised HID devices, or a connected Razer keyboard to re-map.
wiz.probeIdle: Pick a device to check whether it speaks the Razer protocol.
wiz.readOnlyNote: The check only read firmware and serial. Next, choose the layout the keyboard is closest to.
wiz.remapNote: KeyHalo pauses its lighting on this keyboard while you map it. Experimental definitions never replace a verified one for the same device.
wiz.optLampArray: If the keyboard supports Windows Dynamic Lighting it already works through it — check Settings → Personalization → Dynamic Lighting.
wiz.optOpenRgb: If OpenRGB supports it, enable the OpenRGB bridge on the Devices page.
wiz.optRequest: Open a prefilled request with the USB IDs so someone with protocol knowledge can help.
wiz.layoutHint: Pick the physical layout closest to your keyboard, then the size of its LED matrix.
wiz.mapPrompt: One LED is lit on your keyboard. Press that key (or click it below). Nothing lit? Choose “No key is lit”.
wiz.notOnTemplate: {key} is not on this template — click the closest key instead.
wiz.physicalTip: Fn and keys the OS can’t see: click them.
wiz.simHint: No hardware in the browser: this is what the simulated Huntsman Mini is lighting right now.
wiz.simNone: Column 0 of the Huntsman Mini has no LED — choose “No key is lit”.
wiz.reviewHint: {mapped} of {total} template keys mapped. Run the live test and watch the colours sweep across your keyboard.
wiz.saveHint: Adds the definition to KeyHalo and rescans devices.
wiz.saveText: Save it, then check it on the Devices page.
wiz.savedText: KeyHalo now knows this keyboard. Check it on the Devices page.
wiz.publishHint: Opens a pull request so everyone with this keyboard gets support.
wiz.signInFirst: Sign in with GitHub in Community → Share & publish, then come back.
wiz.simNothing: Nothing is lit on the simulated keyboard right now.
